content.comment_body: Hello, I've been using [product_name] from [version_no] for Linux for my business without issues. After the release of the new [product_name] hardware, my old software ([version_no]) showed an error: A newer software version is required. I downloaded [version_no] from [company_name]'s site and upgraded. Installation on my Linux system completed without problems, but when launching [product_name] [version_no], the program starts with no menus or controls, then freezes. I need to force-stop it, as closing via the window does not work. There are no console error messages and I can't identify any debugging options. I edited entries in the configuration file to redirect output and errors to the console. I attached a screenshot of my console and the software window with missing menus/controls. For additional context, I'm using Linux Debian Sid. The download page claims Linux support for Suse Linux, so I also installed OpenSuse [version_no] in a VM and encountered the same issue there—the software does not work on either distribution. I'm looking for help to resolve this issue.
Hello [user_name], Please refer to this thread: [url] Hope this assists you. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi, Thanks [user_name]! I had previously experimented by replacing the jre directory with a symlink to the one in my sun-java directory. Removing the jre directory also works. The software now starts normally, so that's progress. On to the next issue...[snip] New question: Second issue with [product_name] [version_no] for Linux 64bit – Connection to hardware: solved.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced major startup problems with [product_name] [version_no] on Linux, including missing menus and application freezing. Previous software worked without issue, but upgrading revealed incompatibility likely related to the bundled Java runtime. Modifications to the jre directory allowed successful startup.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect new software versions to run reliably on supported Linux distributions, and anticipate a smooth upgrade path to maintain compatibility with newly released hardware, without encountering serious problems.
